judge.role: independent judge over the finished out-of-style control results; Spark saw only the numbers copied from the cited file

metric: gap_closed = (config - base) / (full_delta - base) on mean target logprob over the combined 96 held-out questions

claims.text: The out-of-style adapter is the identical artifact shape to the in-style adapter (rank 17, all seven block linears x 24 blocks, no embedding, 18,696,192 B fp16) and was trained with the identical recipe and seed 20261028; only the distillation prompt set changed (1,500 Gemini-authored prompts, varied surface style, vs 1,500 Spark-authored prompts in the Spark eval style).

On the untouched Spark 96: base -11.1498, full delta -8.5425, uniform -11.0956 (gap closed 0.021), lite -10.5451 (gap closed 0.232), in-style adapter -7.5126 (gap closed 1.395), out-of-style adapter -9.5325 (gap closed 0.620).

Under the interpretation rule frozen in results/lora_outofstyle_design.md before training (>= 0.60 the win is not only style; 0.40-0.60 partly; < 0.40 mostly style), the out-of-style gap closed of 0.620 gives the verdict: survives.

Mirrored eval on the Gemini-authored 96: the full fine-tune scores BELOW the base there (base -9.8679, full -11.3424), so mirror gap closed is recorded as null (negative denominator) and the read is on raw mean logprob: in-style adapter -7.2574 beats the out-of-style adapter -10.1504 on the Gemini set too, so crossover (each adapter wins on its own author's set) is False.

First-token vs continuation split on the Spark 96: in-style adapter mean first-token logprob -5.6539 and continuation -1.8587 (first-token accuracy 0.167); out-of-style adapter first-token -7.5153 and continuation -2.0173 (first-token accuracy 0.042).

Verification: the zero adapter in the new workdir reproduces the stored base per-item logprobs with max abs diff 0.00e+00; the dense W+B@A reference matches the hooked path at 9.66e-06; every published aggregate was recomputed from per-item rows by an independent script (worst stored-vs-recomputed diff 0.00e+00).

Hygiene: the control adapter trained only on the 1,350 Gemini train prompts (150 more used only for early stopping) with teacher-generated supervision; the Spark 96 and the Gemini mirror-96 were never used for training, stopping, or selection; the design, thresholds, and interpretation rule were frozen in results/lora_outofstyle_design.md before any training, after consults with Spark, Gemini, Nemotron, and Glimmer.

headline_question.sentence: Distilled on Gemini-authored prompts in a deliberately different style, the same 18.7 MB LoRA adapter still closes 62.0% of the base-to-full gap on the Spark-written 96 (vs 139.5% in-style and 23.2% for the factored patch), so the adapter's matched-byte win is not only a style-match artifact, though training-style match still adds a large share on top.
